verdict.rationale: Unity's scripting API and editor extensibility allow developers to write event-driven callbacks (e.g., custom C# scripts, Editor Windows) and Build Automation can trigger CI builds on version-control events, which constitutes rudimentary event-triggered automation. However, there is no dedicated no-code/AI-native 'rules engine' where a user defines trigger-action rules declaratively; the closest AI-facing feature (MCP server/Assistant) is prompt-driven action execution rather than persistent event-based rule automation. Missing for 10: a documented declarative rules/trigger-action framework, AI-native example of defining event-based automation, and independent confirmation of such a feature working end-to-end.
